subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make periodic memory index sync a non-zero default fallback for unconfigured users, or keep it opt-in and solve watcher staleness another way?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the likely fix changes default background indexing behavior for existing users and carries compatibility/cost tradeoffs that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Accept default fallback
options.body: Resolve the conflict in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90019 and land the non-zero interval fallback with explicit intervalMinutes: 0 opt-out and docs.

options.title: Keep fallback opt-in
options.body: Keep the default at 0 and require a narrower watcher-health or warning fix, accepting that default users may remain exposed to silent missed events.

options.title: Request a different repair shape
options.body: Ask for watcher restart/liveness detection plus targeted logging before changing any default sync cadence.

recommendation.title: Accept default fallback
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflict in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90019 and land the non-zero interval fallback with explicit intervalMinutes: 0 opt-out and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history signal on the memory engine and memory-core ownership boundary involved in the product default choice.
